content:
We, the PKU AI for Math team, have produced a complete formalization of the Poincaré Conjecture in Lean 4, following the Morgan–Tian exposition of Perelman's proof. :tada: :tada: :tada:

The formalization passes both the Lean build and Comparator against a statement written using only Mathlib definitions, with propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as the only axioms.

Most of the work was completed within half a month by mathematicians collaborating with AI agents. Three AI developers with mathematical backgrounds designed, built, and ran the agentic pipelines, together with several volunteer mathematicians, all using publicly available commercial large language models. The project produced approximately 3.2 million lines of code, at a total cost of less than $30,000 for LLM usage and compute servers. The proof rests on Riemannian and differential geometry, and also draws on topology and partial differential equations. Much of this foundation had not been formalized before, so all prerequisite theory was formalized within the project.

Together with Anthropic's formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem, we see this as the beginning of a new era in formalization: large-scale formal verification of proofs built on extensive theoretical foundations can now be completed in a relatively short time, at a cost affordable to some academic institutions—though not yet cheap enough to be accessible to everyone.

This matters because AI now helps produce far more proofs than ever, making verification more necessary than ever. Verifying all new proofs requires much lower costs, which calls for reusable infrastructure that shortens the distance from existing formalization to frontier proofs. Our current code quality is still far from this goal, and we are committed to improving it toward reusable, high-quality infrastructure. We envision formalization becoming part of daily mathematical practice, helping mathematicians check their own work, fix errors, and sharpen definitions, while greatly accelerating review.

We would also like to congratulate DifferentialGeometry and contributors: Ziyang Qin, Yuan Liao, Bennett Chow, Ayush Khaitan, and Jack McCarthy (please correct us if this list is inaccurate) on their simultaneous independent Lean 4 formalization of Poincare conjecture, released earlier today, which passes the Lean build. We do not yet know whether it has passed Comparator.

Code: https://github.com/frenzymath/PoincareConjecture
News: https://frenzymath.com/news/poincare-formalization/

More details will be shared in a blog post soon.
Discussion thread at #general > Formalizing Poincare Conjecture

Our detailed blog post/technical report is on https://frenzymath.com/blog/poincare-formalization/, with an arxiv version. During the preparation of the blog post, we are doing the initial round of code quality improvement; the length of the code decreased from 3.2M to 2.8M.
